purpose: Project-wide record of the CFM fragmentation failure: every generation pool on disk re-scored with the trainer's own decode_chemistry, joined with the SSOT's per-run rows, and SPLIT by which code path wrote the pool so a decoder reconstruction is never reported as a generator measurement.
direction: single_fragment_ratio (over the parsed rows) and single_molecule_rate (over ALL rows) are the fraction of the pool that is ONE connected molecule -- HIGHER IS BETTER.  fragmented_ratio is the complement -- LOWER IS BETTER.

thresholds.basis: declared policy, not a discovered optimum; the measured calibration anchor is the decoder's own single_fragment_ratio on REAL clouds (0.9375 on the c8 val cohort) against the same run's generation side (0.348)

pipeline_classification.rule: read from the CSV HEADER (and, for a 'metal_z' pool, the CONTENT of its first data row), not the run name: an explicit 'pool_kind' column is authoritative; 'n_frags_raw' in the header is the trainer's free-generation path; a 'metal_z' header is decided by its content (sanitized == 1 and metal_z non-empty -> reconstruction; sanitized == 0 and metal_z empty -> generation); both markers, a missing row or disagreeing signals -> unknown

measurement_meaning.generation: the sampler's free generation: the fraction of the model's own output that is ONE connected molecule -- true of BOTH free-generation writers (the trainer's own path and the 2026-10-12+ ODE path of wf_cfm_decode_dump_smiles.py)
measurement_meaning.reconstruction: era A: the bond head applied to REAL tmQM geometries (the pre-2026-10-12 decode-dump path): the DECODER's fidelity to real chemistry, NOT a fragmentation rate of the generator
measurement_meaning.unknown: the pool's CSV does not establish which code path wrote it (no marker, contradictory markers, or a missing / disagreeing content signal); treat the numbers as unclassified

project_generation_baseline.population: CLEAN runs only: contiguous-from-zero epoch history AND no nan train_loss. The all-runs distribution is in `gen_single_molecule_rate_end_all_runs`; the excluded runs are named in `degenerate_runs_excluded_from_the_headline`
project_generation_baseline.basis: the runs' own trainer-side generation eval: gen_validity_end x gen_single_fragment_ratio_end is the end-to-end rate of ONE connected molecule per sample

retracted_numbers.0.572276953125: WITHDRAWN. It is cfm_r11_eval256's end-to-end rate — a run with ONE recorded epoch (index 19) of a declared 20, resumed above epoch 0, train_loss nan. The JSON value of the same cell is 0.572265625; 0.572276953125 is the 4-decimal CSV rendering. It is the max of the ALL-RUNS distribution, not of the clean-run headline.

project_generation_baseline.cohort_axis_is_unresolved: the n_train axis (256 vs 26715) is UNRESOLVED: the ordering flips with the READING and with the BUDGET, so no cohort median is a bar. See metrics/by_metric/cfm_run_census.json -> budget_matched.ordering_flips and by_n_train.

recorded_vs_rederived.recorded_last_epoch_source: cfm_run_census.json:runs[c7_fullgen_smoke_2026_10_20].gen_single_fragment_ratio_end -- the run's LAST-epoch aggregate; its epoch is the census's own integrity.epoch_index_end
recorded_vs_rederived.note: BOTH sides of this cross-check now refer to the POOL'S OWN EPOCH: the recorded value is the resolved population's aggregate row at that epoch, and the re-derivation is over every SMILES row of the pool file -- which, for a multi-epoch pool, spans EVERY epoch the pool covers, not only its last one.  A non-zero difference is therefore expected and is NOT a mismatch by itself.  For a RECONSTRUCTION pool the two numbers are not even the same measurement, so the difference carries no information about the generator.  The run's LAST-epoch value is kept beside this one, labelled with its own epoch, because it is a DIFFERENT measurement: it describes the run's final epoch, not the epoch these molecules were drawn at.  When the run's last epoch IS the pool's own epoch (MEASURED: it is, for both census-less runs) the two measurements coincide BY CONSTRUCTION -- they are two readings of the same epoch, not one copied from the other -- and recorded_last_epoch_equals_pool_epoch says so explicitly.
